segmentation.text: about to enter or exit a controlled-access highway
to all vehicles approaching on the highway
whose proximity constitutes an immediate hazard
and shall continue to yield the right-of-way to that traffic until the driver may proceed with reasonable safety.

elements.justification: Vehicle aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; the driver read through the vehicle's controlled motion.

st.controlled_access 'a highway with access only at designated points, and its entrance and exit lanes' (DEF-NRS-484A-060 'no legal right of access except at such points only'). 'About to' is an imminent movement, read by the movement it leads to: the entry (x's footprint begins to overlap the controlled-access region, rel.occupies 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region ... controlled-access lane') or the exit (it ceases to overlap it, onto another st.highway region).

Yielding is not making the entry or exit (the change of x's overlap with the controlled-access region, rel.occupies) while moving (drv.motion.moving) into a predicted conflict with a vehicle owed precedence.

All vehicles y (aggregate) approaching on the highway: y moving (drv.motion.moving) with its footprint on the highway being entered - the controlled-access region at an entry, the st.highway region x moves onto at an exit (rel.occupies).

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way (DEF-NRS-484A-210: 'circumstances of direction, speed and proximity as to give rise to the danger of a crash')
operationalizations.convention: Traffic-conflict technique: the danger of a crash is a predicted closest approach of the two centres under constant velocities within the time-to-collision horizon at a centre distance below the clearance.

operationalizations.standard: whose proximity constitutes an immediate hazard
operationalizations.convention: Gap acceptance for merging: a vehicle on the highway is an immediate hazard where the gap between the bodies (rel.surface_gap 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies') is at most its speed (kin.speed) times the critical gap, so the bound moves with its speed.

applicability: x is a vehicle. Judged at each entry of x into a controlled-access region a (st.controlled_access): an observation at which x's footprint overlaps a and did not at the observation before; and at each exit: an observation at which x's footprint no longer overlaps a and did at the observation before; where there is a vehicle y other than x on the highway being entered - at an entry, y's footprint overlaps a; at an exit, y's footprint overlaps a st.highway region that x's footprint overlaps at that observation, and not a - that is moving (drv.motion.moving with p.motion_speed_tolerance) and whose body gap to x (rel.surface_gap) is at most its speed (kin.speed) times p.immediate_hazard_time_gap.
obligation: Where x is moving at the judged observation (drv.motion.moving with p.motion_speed_tolerance), no vehicle y of the applicability (bound again with its whole selection) has its centre and x's approach within p.conflict_time_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance).

narrowings.why: The driver is read through the vehicle's controlled motion.
'About to enter or exit' is an imminent movement, read by the movement it leads to: the observation of entry into, or exit from, the controlled-access region.
The yield is judged at the observation of entry or exit; 'the highway' is read as the highway being entered: the controlled-access highway at an entry, the highway x moves onto at an exit.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: x enters controlled-access region a from an adjoining way at 15 m/s while y on a is 12 m away at 28 m/s (12 m below 28 m/s times the critical gap); predicted closest approach 1.5 m in 0.8 s.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: x enters a while y on a, 60 m behind at 25 m/s (within speed times the critical gap), is predicted to pass in the next lane 6 m from x at its closest.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: x drives on an ordinary roadway and never enters or leaves a controlled-access region.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, but rel.surface_gap is not supplied and cannot be computed (kin.extent absent), so whether y's proximity is an immediate hazard is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: x leaves a onto a crossroad (st.highway) and moves across it while y on the crossroad, 10 m away at 13 m/s, is in predicted conflict (1 m in 0.9 s).

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: x enters a with no other road user in the scene.

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_time_horizon
param_proposals.convention: Time-to-collision horizon of the traffic-conflict technique: a predicted closest approach within this time counts as an imminent conflict.
param_proposals.source: Hayward (1972) time-to-collision; Swedish Traffic Conflict Technique (Hyden 1987)

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: Centre-to-centre distance at the predicted closest approach below which two road users' bodies come into conflict: about a passenger car's half-length plus a crossing road user's half-length with a small margin, since the distance is between reference points.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO Green Book passenger-car design vehicle dimensions

param_proposals.name: p.immediate_hazard_time_gap
param_proposals.convention: Critical gap of gap acceptance: an approaching vehicle whose time to reach the conflict (its distance over its speed) is at most this gap is an immediate hazard to a turning, crossing or merging manoeuvre.
param_proposals.source: Highway Capacity Manual, base critical headway (4.1 s for a major-street left turn)

param_proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
param_proposals.source: Speed-estimate noise of the acquisition standard (carla_scene_graph kinematics)
